VI. When the Determinant Bound Is Attained

The conditional content of any admissible description is bounded below by a determinant expression, and it is natural to ask when the bound is exact. The question is sharpest for a joint description serving two described variables, and this section settles it there; the single-variable answer appears as a corollary inside the proof. In this section only, Y=(YA,YB)Y=(Y_A,Y_B) denotes a pair of normalized described variables of the source, jointly Gaussian with the normalized context VV, with an arbitrary correlation pattern; the third party again holds S=V+US=V+U, U∼𝒩(0,τ2)U\sim\mathcal N(0,\tau^2), with XX, UU, and all channel randomness mutually independent. A joint channel produces 𝐘̂=(ŶA,ŶB)\hat{\mathbf Y}=(\widehat{Y}_A,\widehat{Y}_B) with 𝐘̂−X−S\hat{\mathbf Y}-X-S and must meet 𝔼(YA−ŶA)2≤DA\mathbb{E}(Y_A-\widehat{Y}_A)^2\le D_A and 𝔼(YB−ŶB)2≤DB\mathbb{E}(Y_B-\widehat{Y}_B)^2\le D_B; write Lmin(DA,DB)=min⁡I(X;𝐘̂∣S)L_{\min}(D_A,D_B)=\min I(X;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S).

Write ΣY\Sigma_Y for the covariance of the pair YY, β=Cov⁡(Y,V)∈ℝ2\beta=\operatorname{Cov}(Y,V)\in\mathbb{R}^2, ΣY∣V=ΣY−ββ𝖳\Sigma_{Y\mid V}=\Sigma_Y-\beta\beta^{\mathsf T}, ΣY∣S=ΣY−ββ𝖳/(1+τ2)\Sigma_{Y\mid S}=\Sigma_Y-\beta\beta^{\mathsf T}/(1{+}\tau^2), and Δ=diag(DA,DB)≻0\Delta=\mathrm{diag}(D_A,D_B)\succ0. Define the determinant lower bound 𝖡det:=12log⁡2det⁡ΣY∣Sdet⁡Δ,\mathsf{B}_{\det}:=\tfrac12\log_2\frac{\det\Sigma_{Y\mid S}}{\det\Delta}\,, which can be negative at large distortions. Every admissible channel obeys L≥I(Y;𝐘̂∣S)=h(Y∣S)−h(Y∣𝐘̂,S)≥𝖡det,henceL≥[𝖡det]+:=max⁡{𝖡det,0},(41)\begin{equation*} L\;\ge\;I(Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S) \;=\;h(Y\mid S)-h(Y\mid\hat{\mathbf Y},S) \;\ge\;\mathsf{B}_{\det}, \qquad\text{hence}\qquad L\;\ge\;\bigl[\mathsf{B}_{\det}\bigr]^{+}:=\max\{\mathsf{B}_{\det},0\}, \qquad\text{(41)} \end{equation*} since h(Y∣S)=12log⁡2((2πe)2det⁡ΣY∣S)h(Y\mid S)=\tfrac12\log_2\bigl((2\pi e)^2\det\Sigma_{Y\mid S}\bigr), h(Y∣𝐘̂,S)≤∑i∈{A,B}h(Yi−Ŷi)≤12log⁡2((2πe)2DADB)h(Y\mid\hat{\mathbf Y},S)\le\sum_{i\in\{A,B\}}h(Y_i-\widehat{Y}_i) \le\tfrac12\log_2\bigl((2\pi e)^2 D_AD_B\bigr), and L≥0L\ge0 always.1 The exactness question below concerns 𝖡det\mathsf{B}_{\det} itself: on the attainment branches of Theorem 20 the semidefinite conditions force det⁡Δ≤det⁡ΣY∣S\det\Delta\le\det\Sigma_{Y\mid S}, so there 𝖡det≥0\mathsf{B}_{\det}\ge0 and the two forms agree; where 𝖡det<0\mathsf{B}_{\det}<0, attainment fails trivially since Lmin≥0L_{\min}\ge0.

Three facts from the machinery already built carry over. First, pair sufficiency extends verbatim: the resampling proof of Theorem 7 applies with T=(YA,YB,V)T=(Y_A,Y_B,V), since S=V+US=V+U with UU jointly independent of (X,all channel randomness)(X,\text{all channel randomness}) and the distortions are functionals of the pairs (Yi,Ŷi)(Y_i,\widehat{Y}_i); so the channel may be restricted to depend on XX only through TT, and then I(X;𝐘̂∣S)=I(T;𝐘̂∣S)I(X;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S)=I(T;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S). Second, the same mutual independence forces the Markov moment identity Cov⁡(S,𝐘̂)=Cov⁡(V,𝐘̂)\operatorname{Cov}(S,\hat{\mathbf Y})=\operatorname{Cov}(V,\hat{\mathbf Y}). Third, for τ2>0\tau^2>0, jointly Gaussian channels 𝐘̂=AT+N\hat{\mathbf Y}=AT+N, N∼𝒩(0,ΣN)N\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_N), exhaust the problem, by Lemma 9: for any admissible TT-channel with C=Cov⁡(T,𝐘̂)C=\operatorname{Cov}(T,\hat{\mathbf Y}) and ΣŶ=Cov⁡(𝐘̂)\Sigma_{\hat Y}=\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mathbf Y}), set A:=C𝖳ΣT−1A:=C^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_T^{-1} and ΣN:=ΣŶ−AΣTA𝖳≽0\Sigma_N:=\Sigma_{\hat Y}-A\Sigma_TA^{\mathsf T}\succeq0 (assume ΣT≻0\Sigma_T\succ0; degenerate instances reduce by dropping dependent context components; singular ΣN\Sigma_N is dispatched by Remark 10, whereby a singular residual either reveals a noiseless linear functional of TT, making every bound trivial, or has a removable zero component). The lemma’s positivity hypothesis Cov⁡((T,S))≻0\operatorname{Cov}((T,S))\succ0 holds exactly when τ2>0\tau^2>0, since ΣS∣T=τ2\Sigma_{S\mid T}=\tau^2; the boundary τ2=0\tau^2=0, where S=VS=V is a coordinate of TT and the joint covariance is singular, is treated separately by Lemma 19 below. The residual 𝐘̂−AT\hat{\mathbf Y}-AT is uncorrelated with TT, hence with VV, and with UU by mutual independence, hence with SS, so for τ2>0\tau^2>0 L≥12log⁡2det⁡(AΣT∣SA𝖳+ΣN)det⁡ΣN,ΣT∣S=ΣT−σTSσTS𝖳1+τ2,σTS=ΣTeV,(42)\begin{equation*} L\;\ge\;\tfrac12\log_2 \frac{\det\bigl(A\Sigma_{T\mid S}A^{\mathsf T}+\Sigma_N\bigr)} {\det\Sigma_N}, \qquad \Sigma_{T\mid S} =\Sigma_T-\frac{\sigma_{TS}\sigma_{TS}^{\mathsf T}}{1+\tau^2}, \quad \sigma_{TS}=\Sigma_Te_V, \qquad\text{(42)} \end{equation*} with equality for the jointly Gaussian channel realizing the same moments, and the distortion constraints (ei−Ai⋅)𝖳ΣT(ei−Ai⋅)+(ΣN)ii≤Di(e_i-A_{i\cdot})^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_T(e_i-A_{i\cdot})+(\Sigma_N)_{ii}\le D_i depend on the channel only through those moments.

LminL_{\min} is attained. The feasible set ℱ={(A,ΣN):ΣN≽0,(ei−Ai⋅)𝖳ΣT(ei−Ai⋅)+(ΣN)ii≤Di,i∈{A,B}}\mathcal F=\bigl\{(A,\Sigma_N):\Sigma_N\succeq0,\ (e_i-A_{i\cdot})^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_T(e_i-A_{i\cdot}) +(\Sigma_N)_{ii}\le D_i,\ i\in\{A,B\}\bigr\} is compact: the quadratic constraints confine the rows of AA to ellipsoids (ΣT≻0\Sigma_T\succ0), the diagonal of ΣN\Sigma_N is bounded by (DA,DB)(D_A,D_B), and the off-diagonal obeys (ΣN)AB2≤(ΣN)AA(ΣN)BB≤DADB(\Sigma_N)_{AB}^2\le(\Sigma_N)_{AA}(\Sigma_N)_{BB}\le D_AD_B. The map (A,ΣN)↦I(T;AT+N∣S)=I(T;(AT+N,S))−I(T;S)(A,\Sigma_N)\mapsto I(T;AT+N\mid S)=I\bigl(T;(AT+N,S)\bigr)-I(T;S) is lower semicontinuous on ℱ\mathcal F: the second term is a constant, the joint Gaussian law of (T,AT+N,S)(T,AT+N,S) is weakly continuous in (A,ΣN)(A,\Sigma_N), and mutual information is lower semicontinuous under weak convergence of the joint law [8]. A minimizing sequence therefore has a cluster point in ℱ\mathcal F at which the infimum is attained.

A plausible conjecture states the attainment condition for 𝖡det\mathsf{B}_{\det} through the third party’s conditional covariance ΣY∣S\Sigma_{Y\mid S}; the truth involves the encoder-accessible ΣY∣V\Sigma_{Y\mid V}, the same SS-versus-VV substitution as in Proposition 8. For the unconditional Gaussian vector source under individual distortion constraints, the exact tightness condition of the determinant (Hadamard-type) lower bound on the rate has recently been settled by Chen et al. [16]: the bound is tight precisely when a semidefinite condition of the form Δ≼Σ\Delta\preceq\Sigma holds. Conditions (a) and (b) of Theorem 20 instantiate exactly that condition, on the conditional covariance ΣY∣V\Sigma_{Y\mid V} and on ΣY\Sigma_Y respectively; the new content here is which covariance carries it, namely the encoder-accessible one, decided by the conditioner’s noise.

Lemma 19 (Clean-context reduction). Let τ2=0\tau^2=0, so S=VS=V almost surely, and assume Σc:=ΣY∣V≻0\Sigma_c:=\Sigma_{Y\mid V}\succ0. Write Ỹ:=Y−βV\widetilde Y:=Y-\beta V, which is independent of VV with covariance Σc\Sigma_c, and let Rc(DA,DB):=min⁡{I(Ỹ;𝐘̂′):𝔼(Ỹi−Ŷi′)2≤Di,i∈{A,B}}R_c(D_A,D_B):=\min\bigl\{I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}'):\ \mathbb{E}(\widetilde Y_i-\widehat{Y}_i')^2\le D_i,\ i\in\{A,B\}\bigr\} be the unconditional minimum for the pair source Ỹ∼𝒩(0,Σc)\widetilde Y\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_c). Then Lmin(DA,DB)=Rc(DA,DB),L_{\min}(D_A,D_B)\;=\;R_c(D_A,D_B), and the determinant lower bound is attained at τ2=0\tau^2=0, namely Lmin=𝖡det=12log⁡2(det⁡Σc/det⁡Δ)L_{\min}=\mathsf{B}_{\det}=\tfrac12\log_2(\det\Sigma_c/\det\Delta), if and only if Δ≼Σc\Delta\preceq\Sigma_c; otherwise Lmin>𝖡detL_{\min}>\mathsf{B}_{\det} [15], [16].

Proof. Reduction of the objective. Cov⁡(Ỹ,V)=β−β=0\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde Y,V)=\beta-\beta=0 and (Ỹ,V)(\widetilde Y,V) is jointly Gaussian, so Ỹ⟂V\widetilde Y\perp V. The map (Y,V)↔(Ỹ,V)(Y,V)\leftrightarrow(\widetilde Y,V) is a linear bijection, so for every channel I(T;𝐘̂∣V)=I((Ỹ,V);𝐘̂∣V)=I(Ỹ;𝐘̂∣V)I(T;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid V) =I\bigl((\widetilde Y,V);\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid V\bigr) =I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid V).

Disintegration and recentering. By the per-ss decomposition (as in Lemma 3, through a regular conditional probability), I(Ỹ;𝐘̂∣V)=∫IvdPV(v)I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid V)=\int I_v\,dP_V(v) and 𝔼(Yi−Ŷi)2=∫Di(v)dPV(v)\mathbb{E}(Y_i-\widehat{Y}_i)^2=\int D_i(v)\,dP_V(v) with Di(v):=𝔼[(Yi−Ŷi)2∣V=v]D_i(v):=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(Y_i-\widehat{Y}_i)^2\mid V=v\bigr], where IvI_v is the mutual information of (Ỹ,𝐘̂)(\widetilde Y,\hat{\mathbf Y}) under the conditional law given V=vV=v. Under that law Ỹ∼𝒩(0,Σc)\widetilde Y\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_c), independently of vv. The deterministic shift 𝐘̂′:=𝐘̂−βv\hat{\mathbf Y}':=\hat{\mathbf Y}-\beta v changes neither IvI_v nor the errors, Yi−Ŷi=Ỹi−Ŷi′Y_i-\widehat{Y}_i=\widetilde Y_i-\widehat{Y}_i', so each conditional ensemble is an admissible channel for the source 𝒩(0,Σc)\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_c) at distortion pair (DA(v),DB(v))(D_A(v),D_B(v)), whence Iv≥Rc(DA(v),DB(v))I_v\ge R_c\bigl(D_A(v),D_B(v)\bigr).

Convexity in the distortion pair. RcR_c is nonincreasing in each argument and jointly convex (mix the optimal channels of two distortion pairs; mutual information is convex in the channel at fixed input). By Jensen and monotonicity, I(Ỹ;𝐘̂∣V)≥∫Rc(DA(v),DB(v))dPV(v)≥Rc(∫DAdPV,∫DBdPV)≥Rc(DA,DB).I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid V) \;\ge\;\int R_c\bigl(D_A(v),D_B(v)\bigr)dP_V(v) \;\ge\;R_c\Bigl(\textstyle\int D_A\,dP_V,\int D_B\,dP_V\Bigr) \;\ge\;R_c(D_A,D_B).

Achievability. Let p(𝐲̂′∣ỹ)p(\hat{\mathbf y}'\mid\tilde y) attain Rc(DA,DB)R_c(D_A,D_B); it exists by the SS-deleted instance of the compactness and lower-semicontinuity argument above. Set 𝐘̂:=𝐘̂′+βV\hat{\mathbf Y}:=\hat{\mathbf Y}'+\beta V with 𝐘̂′\hat{\mathbf Y}' drawn from p(⋅∣Ỹ)p(\cdot\mid\widetilde Y) using channel randomness independent of VV. This is an admissible channel (a function of XX and fresh noise; the Markov chain is trivial at S=VS=V), its distortions are 𝔼(Ỹi−Ŷi′)2≤Di\mathbb{E}(\widetilde Y_i-\widehat{Y}_i')^2\le D_i, and given V=vV=v the pair (Ỹ,𝐘̂)(\widetilde Y,\hat{\mathbf Y}) is (Ỹ,𝐘̂′+βv)(\widetilde Y,\hat{\mathbf Y}'+\beta v), so I(Ỹ;𝐘̂∣V)=I(Ỹ;𝐘̂′)=Rc(DA,DB)I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid V) =I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}')=R_c(D_A,D_B). Hence Lmin=Rc(DA,DB)L_{\min}=R_c(D_A,D_B), attained.

The tightness condition. At τ2=0\tau^2=0, ΣY∣S=Σc\Sigma_{Y\mid S}=\Sigma_c, so 𝖡det=12log⁡2(det⁡Σc/det⁡Δ)\mathsf{B}_{\det}=\tfrac12\log_2(\det\Sigma_c/ \det\Delta). Sufficiency: if Δ≼Σc\Delta\preceq\Sigma_c, take 𝐘̂′∼𝒩(0,Σc−Δ)\hat{\mathbf Y}'\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_c-\Delta) and Z∼𝒩(0,Δ)Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Delta) independent with Ỹ=𝐘̂′+Z\widetilde Y=\hat{\mathbf Y}'+Z (the reverse channel; the required covariances are Σc−Δ≽0\Sigma_c-\Delta\succeq0 and Δ≻0\Delta\succ0, no further condition). Its distortions are DiD_i exactly, and since Ỹ∣𝐘̂′∼𝒩(𝐘̂′,Δ)\widetilde Y\mid\hat{\mathbf Y}'\sim\mathcal N(\hat{\mathbf Y}',\Delta), I(Ỹ;𝐘̂′)=h(Ỹ)−h(Ỹ∣𝐘̂′)=12log⁡2((2πe)2det⁡Σc)−12log⁡2((2πe)2det⁡Δ)=𝖡det.I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}') =h(\widetilde Y)-h(\widetilde Y\mid\hat{\mathbf Y}') =\tfrac12\log_2\bigl((2\pi e)^2\det\Sigma_c\bigr) -\tfrac12\log_2\bigl((2\pi e)^2\det\Delta\bigr) =\mathsf{B}_{\det}. Necessity: suppose some channel attains I(Ỹ;𝐘̂′)=𝖡detI(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}')=\mathsf{B}_{\det}, and write Z′:=Ỹ−𝐘̂′Z':=\widetilde Y-\hat{\mathbf Y}'. In the chain 𝖡det=I(Ỹ;𝐘̂′)=h(Ỹ)−h(Z′∣𝐘̂′)≥h(Ỹ)−h(Z′)≥h(Ỹ)−h(ZA′)−h(ZB′)≥𝖡det,\mathsf{B}_{\det}=I(\widetilde Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}') =h(\widetilde Y)-h\bigl(Z'\mid\hat{\mathbf Y}'\bigr) \ \ge\ h(\widetilde Y)-h(Z') \ \ge\ h(\widetilde Y)-h(Z'_A)-h(Z'_B) \ \ge\ \mathsf{B}_{\det}, equality in conditioning-reduces-entropy, in subadditivity, and in the Gaussian maximum-entropy bound forces Z′⟂𝐘̂′Z'\perp\hat{\mathbf Y}' with Z′∼𝒩(0,Δ)Z'\sim\mathcal N(0,\Delta) (the same three-step equality analysis spelled out in the necessity part of Theorem 20’s proof below); then Cov⁡(𝐘̂′)=Σc−Δ≽0\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mathbf Y}')=\Sigma_c-\Delta\succeq0, that is, Δ≼Σc\Delta\preceq\Sigma_c. Since RcR_c is attained, Lmin>𝖡detL_{\min}>\mathsf{B}_{\det} whenever Δ⋠Σc\Delta\not\preceq\Sigma_c.

□

Theorem 20 (Consequence: determinant-bound exactness). The determinant lower bound is attained, Lmin=𝖡detL_{\min}=\mathsf{B}_{\det}, iff (a) τ2=0 and Δ≼ΣY∣V,or(b) β=0 and Δ≼ΣY.\text{(a) } \tau^2=0 \text{ and } \Delta\preceq\Sigma_{Y\mid V}, \qquad\text{or}\qquad \text{(b) } \beta=0 \text{ and } \Delta\preceq\Sigma_Y . In every other case the bound is strict, both on the misaligned branch (τ2>0\tau^2>0 and β≠0\beta\ne0, at every positive (DA,DB)(D_A,D_B)) and outside the semidefinite conditions of (a) and (b). On the misaligned branch with Δ≺ΣY∣V\Delta\prec\Sigma_{Y\mid V}, the deficit obeys the sandwich 0<Lmin−𝖡det≤12log⁡2det⁡(I−ΣY∣S−1Δ)det⁡(I−ΣY∣V−1Δ)=12tr⁡[(ΣY∣V−1−ΣY∣S−1)Δ]log⁡2e+O(∥Δ∥2)→0(Δ→0).0\;<\;L_{\min}-\mathsf{B}_{\det}\;\le\; \tfrac12\log_2\frac{\det\bigl(I-\Sigma_{Y\mid S}^{-1}\Delta\bigr)} {\det\bigl(I-\Sigma_{Y\mid V}^{-1}\Delta\bigr)} \;=\;\tfrac12\,\operatorname{tr}\bigl[(\Sigma_{Y\mid V}^{-1}-\Sigma_{Y\mid S}^{-1}) \Delta\bigr]\log_2 e+O(\|\Delta\|^2)\;\longrightarrow\;0 \ \ (\Delta\to0).

Proof. The branch τ2=0\tau^2=0 is Lemma 19: there ΣY∣S=ΣY∣V\Sigma_{Y\mid S}=\Sigma_{Y\mid V}, and Lmin=𝖡detL_{\min}=\mathsf{B}_{\det} iff Δ≼ΣY∣V\Delta\preceq\Sigma_{Y\mid V}, which is condition (a). It remains to treat τ2>0\tau^2>0, where LminL_{\min} is attained by the compactness and lower-semicontinuity argument preceding Lemma 19.

Necessity at τ2>0\tau^2>0: the equality analysis. Suppose a channel attains L=𝖡detL=\mathsf{B}_{\det}. Write Z:=Y−𝐘̂Z:=Y-\hat{\mathbf Y}. The chain (41) reads, term by term, 𝖡det=L≥I(Y;𝐘̂∣S)=h(Y∣S)−h(Z∣𝐘̂,S)≥h(Y∣S)−h(Z)≥h(Y∣S)−h(ZA)−h(ZB)≥𝖡det,\mathsf{B}_{\det}=L\;\ge\;I(Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S) =h(Y\mid S)-h\bigl(Z\mid\hat{\mathbf Y},S\bigr) \;\ge\;h(Y\mid S)-h(Z) \;\ge\;h(Y\mid S)-h(Z_A)-h(Z_B) \;\ge\;\mathsf{B}_{\det}, using h(Y∣𝐘̂,S)=h(Z∣𝐘̂,S)h(Y\mid\hat{\mathbf Y},S)=h(Z\mid\hat{\mathbf Y},S) (translation by the conditioning variable), conditioning reduces entropy, subadditivity, and the Gaussian maximum-entropy bound h(Zi)≤12log⁡2(2πeVar⁡Zi)≤12log⁡2(2πeDi)h(Z_i)\le\tfrac12\log_2\bigl(2\pi e\operatorname{Var}Z_i\bigr) \le\tfrac12\log_2(2\pi eD_i). Equality throughout forces: (i) h(Z∣𝐘̂,S)=h(Z)h(Z\mid\hat{\mathbf Y},S)=h(Z), so I(Z;(𝐘̂,S))=0I\bigl(Z;(\hat{\mathbf Y},S)\bigr)=0 and ZZ is independent of (𝐘̂,S)(\hat{\mathbf Y},S); (ii) h(Z)=h(ZA)+h(ZB)h(Z)=h(Z_A)+h(Z_B), so ZA⟂ZBZ_A\perp Z_B; (iii) each ZiZ_i is Gaussian with variance exactly DiD_i. Hence Z∼𝒩(0,Δ)Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Delta) independent of (𝐘̂,S)(\hat{\mathbf Y},S). No replacement of the channel by a Gaussian one is needed: the equality analysis delivers the Gaussianity of the error directly, and only moments enter below. Consequences at the moment level: Cov⁡Z=Δ\operatorname{Cov}Z=\Delta, Cov⁡(Z,𝐘̂)=0\operatorname{Cov}(Z,\hat{\mathbf Y})=0, Cov⁡(Z,S)=0\operatorname{Cov}(Z,S)=0; also Cov⁡(Z,U)=0\operatorname{Cov}(Z,U)=0 (ZZ is a function of XX and channel noise, UU is independent of both), so Cov⁡(Z,V)=Cov⁡(Z,S)−Cov⁡(Z,U)=0\operatorname{Cov}(Z,V)=\operatorname{Cov}(Z,S)-\operatorname{Cov}(Z,U)=0 and Cov⁡(𝐘̂,V)=Cov⁡(Y,V)−Cov⁡(Z,V)=β\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mathbf Y},V)=\operatorname{Cov}(Y,V)-\operatorname{Cov}(Z,V)=\beta. Moreover Cov⁡(Y,Z)=Cov⁡(𝐘̂+Z,Z)=Δ\operatorname{Cov}(Y,Z)=\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mathbf Y}+Z,Z)=\Delta, so Cov⁡(𝐘̂)=Cov⁡(Y−Z)=ΣY−Δ−Δ+Δ=ΣY−Δ≽0,that is,Δ≼ΣY.\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mathbf Y})=\operatorname{Cov}(Y-Z) =\Sigma_Y-\Delta-\Delta+\Delta=\Sigma_Y-\Delta\;\succeq\;0, \qquad\text{that is,}\qquad \Delta\preceq\Sigma_Y .

Necessity at τ2>0\tau^2>0: the no-leakage condition and the block inversion. Equality of the first step of the chain, L=I(T;𝐘̂∣S)=I(Y;𝐘̂∣S)L=I(T;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S)=I(Y;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S), gives I(V;𝐘̂∣Y,S)=0I(V;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid Y,S)=0: VV and 𝐘̂\hat{\mathbf Y} are conditionally independent given (Y,S)(Y,S). Because (V,Y,S)(V,Y,S) is jointly Gaussian, 𝔼[V∣Y,S]\mathbb{E}[V\mid Y,S] is linear, and the law of total covariance turns conditional independence into a vanishing partial covariance: with Vlin:=𝔼[V∣Y,S]V_{\mathrm{lin}}:=\mathbb{E}[V\mid Y,S] and 𝐘̂lin\hat{\mathbf Y}_{\mathrm{lin}} the best linear estimate of 𝐘̂\hat{\mathbf Y} from (Y,S)(Y,S), pCov⁡(𝐘̂,V):=Cov⁡(𝐘̂−𝐘̂lin,V−Vlin)=𝔼[Cov⁡(𝐘̂,V∣Y,S)]=0,\operatorname{pCov}\bigl(\hat{\mathbf Y},V\bigr) :=\operatorname{Cov}\bigl(\hat{\mathbf Y}-\hat{\mathbf Y}_{\mathrm{lin}},\, V-V_{\mathrm{lin}}\bigr) =\mathbb{E}\bigl[\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mathbf Y},V\mid Y,S)\bigr]=0 , where the cross term of the total-covariance decomposition vanishes identically because VlinV_{\mathrm{lin}} coincides with the conditional mean 𝔼[V∣Y,S]\mathbb{E}[V\mid Y,S] for the jointly Gaussian triple (V,Y,S)(V,Y,S). Now evaluate pCov\operatorname{pCov} from the pinned moments. With M:=Cov⁡((Y,S))=[ΣYββ𝖳s]M:=\operatorname{Cov}\bigl((Y,S)\bigr)= \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}\Sigma_Y&\beta\\ \beta^{\mathsf T}&s\end{smallmatrix}\bigr] (s=1+τ2s=1+\tau^2), Cov⁡(𝐘̂,V)=β\operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\mathbf Y},V)=\beta, Cov⁡(𝐘̂,(Y,S))=[ΣY−Δ,β]\operatorname{Cov}\bigl(\hat{\mathbf Y},(Y,S)\bigr)=[\Sigma_Y-\Delta,\ \beta], and Cov⁡((Y,S),V)=[β;1]\operatorname{Cov}\bigl((Y,S),V\bigr)=[\beta;\,1], pCov⁡(𝐘̂,V)=β−[ΣY−Δ,β]M−1[β1]=β−([I2,0]−[Δ,0]M−1)[β1]=[Δ,0]M−1[β1],\operatorname{pCov}(\hat{\mathbf Y},V) =\beta-[\Sigma_Y-\Delta,\ \beta]\,M^{-1} \begin{bmatrix}\beta\\1\end{bmatrix} =\beta-\bigl([I_2,\ 0]-[\Delta,\ 0]\,M^{-1}\bigr) \begin{bmatrix}\beta\\1\end{bmatrix} =[\Delta,\ 0]\,M^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}\beta\\1\end{bmatrix}, where [ΣY,β]M−1=[I2,0][\Sigma_Y,\ \beta]M^{-1}=[I_2,\ 0] because [ΣY,β][\Sigma_Y,\ \beta] is the first block row of MM. Solve Mw=[β;1]Mw=[\beta;1] by block elimination: writing w=(wY,wS)w=(w_Y,w_S) and ρV2:=β𝖳ΣY−1β\rho_V^2:=\beta^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Y^{-1}\beta (the variance explained by the best linear predictor of VV from YY; ρV2<1\rho_V^2<1 since ΣT≻0\Sigma_T\succ0), ΣYwY+βwS=β,β𝖳wY+swS=1⇒wS=1−ρV2s−ρV2,wY=τ2s−ρV2ΣY−1β,\Sigma_Yw_Y+\beta w_S=\beta,\quad \beta^{\mathsf T}w_Y+sw_S=1 \;\Longrightarrow\; w_S=\frac{1-\rho_V^2}{s-\rho_V^2},\qquad w_Y=\frac{\tau^2}{s-\rho_V^2}\,\Sigma_Y^{-1}\beta, with s−ρV2≥s−1=τ2>0s-\rho_V^2\ge s-1=\tau^2>0. Hence pCov⁡(𝐘̂,V)=ΔwY=τ2s−ρV2ΔΣY−1β,\operatorname{pCov}(\hat{\mathbf Y},V) =\Delta w_Y =\frac{\tau^2}{s-\rho_V^2}\,\Delta\Sigma_Y^{-1}\beta, which vanishes iff τ2=0\tau^2=0 or β=0\beta=0 (Δ≻0\Delta\succ0 and ΣY−1\Sigma_Y^{-1} nonsingular act injectively). On the branch τ2>0\tau^2>0 this forces β=0\beta=0. Combined with Δ≼ΣY\Delta\preceq\Sigma_Y above, attainment at τ2>0\tau^2>0 implies condition (b); attainment at τ2=0\tau^2=0 implies condition (a) by Lemma 19. Necessity is proved.

Sufficiency (a). Lemma 19.

Sufficiency (b). At β=0\beta=0, Y⟂(V,U)Y\perp(V,U), so ΣY∣S=ΣY\Sigma_{Y\mid S}=\Sigma_Y. Take the reverse channel of Lemma 19’s tightness step with ΣY\Sigma_Y in place of Σc\Sigma_c: 𝐘̂∼𝒩(0,ΣY−Δ)\hat{\mathbf Y}\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_Y-\Delta), Z∼𝒩(0,Δ)Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Delta) independent, Y=𝐘̂+ZY=\hat{\mathbf Y}+Z, which exists iff Δ≼ΣY\Delta\preceq\Sigma_Y. The channel depends on XX only through YY, with channel randomness independent of (V,U)(V,U), so 𝐘̂⟂S\hat{\mathbf Y}\perp S and 𝐘̂⟂(V,S)\hat{\mathbf Y}\perp(V,S) given YY; hence I(T;𝐘̂∣S)=h(𝐘̂∣S)−h(𝐘̂∣T,S)=h(𝐘̂)−h(𝐘̂∣Y)=I(Y;𝐘̂)=12log⁡2(det⁡ΣY/det⁡Δ)=𝖡detI(T;\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S)=h(\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid S)-h(\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid T,S)=h(\hat{\mathbf Y})-h(\hat{\mathbf Y}\mid Y) =I(Y;\hat{\mathbf Y})=\tfrac12\log_2\bigl(\det\Sigma_Y/\det\Delta\bigr) =\mathsf{B}_{\det} [15], [16].

Sandwich. At τ2>0\tau^2>0 with Δ≺ΣY∣V\Delta\prec\Sigma_{Y\mid V}, take Z∼𝒩(0,Δ)Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Delta) jointly Gaussian with Cov⁡(Z,Y)=Δ\operatorname{Cov}(Z,Y)=\Delta, Cov⁡(Z,V)=0\operatorname{Cov}(Z,V)=0; such a ZZ exists iff Δ−ΔΣY∣V−1Δ≽0⇔Δ≼ΣY∣V\Delta-\Delta\Sigma_{Y\mid V}^{-1}\Delta\succeq0 \Leftrightarrow\Delta\preceq\Sigma_{Y\mid V} (Schur complement). The channel 𝐘̂=Y−Z\hat{\mathbf Y}=Y-Z yields L≤12log⁡2[det⁡(ΣY∣S−Δ)/det⁡(Δ−ΔΣY∣V−1Δ)]=𝖡det+12log⁡2[det⁡(I−ΣY∣S−1Δ)/det⁡(I−ΣY∣V−1Δ)]L\le\tfrac12\log_2[\det(\Sigma_{Y\mid S}-\Delta)/\det(\Delta- \Delta\Sigma_{Y\mid V}^{-1}\Delta)]=\mathsf{B}_{\det} +\tfrac12\log_2[\det(I-\Sigma_{Y\mid S}^{-1}\Delta)/\det(I- \Sigma_{Y\mid V}^{-1}\Delta)]; the ratio is ≥1\ge1 because ΣY∣S≽ΣY∣V\Sigma_{Y\mid S}\succeq\Sigma_{Y\mid V} (congruence by Δ1/2\Delta^{1/2} keeps both factors in the PSD order where det\det is monotone), and →1\to1 as Δ→0\Delta\to0. Strictness (>0>0) is the necessity direction, using that LminL_{\min} is attained at τ2>0\tau^2>0 (the compactness and lower-semicontinuity argument above).

The single-variable corollary. VIII. The Binary Solution

The binary case closes completely and, unlike its Gaussian counterpart, with an elementary self-contained proof.

Let (Y,V)(Y,V) be a doubly symmetric binary pair (fair marginals, Pr⁡[Y≠V]=p∈(0,12)\Pr[Y\ne V]=p\in(0,\tfrac12)), context VV, side information S=V⊕WS=V\oplus W with W∼Bern(q)W\sim\mathrm{Bern}(q), q∈[0,12]q\in[0,\tfrac12], independent. The description is the reproduction Ŷ∈{0,1}\hat Y\in\{0,1\} itself (richer descriptions only cost more: for any stored ZZ from which the decoder computes Ŷ=f(Z)\hat Y=f(Z), I(Y,V;Z∣S)≥I(Y,V;Ŷ∣S)I(Y,V;Z\mid S)\ge I(Y,V;\hat Y\mid S) by the data-processing inequality), Hamming distortion Pr⁡[Ŷ≠Y]≤D\Pr[\hat Y\ne Y]\le D. Write x*q=x(1−q)+(1−x)qx*q=x(1-q)+(1-x)q and ℓ(x)=ln⁡1−xx\ell(x)=\ln\frac{1-x}{x}.

Lemma 22 (Convexity over the shared channel). L(C):=I(Y,V;Ŷ∣S)L(C):=I(Y,V;\hat Y\mid S) is convex in the channel C=P(ŷ∣y,v)C=P(\hat y\mid y,v), and the Hamming distortion is linear in CC.

Proof. The Markov chain Ŷ−(Y,V)−S\hat Y-(Y,V)-S means that one channel CC is shared across the values of SS, so L(C)=∑sP(s)Is(C)L(C)=\sum_sP(s)\,I_s(C), where Is(C)I_s(C) is the mutual information of the channel CC under the input law P(Y,V∣S=s)P(Y,V\mid S=s). The input laws depend on ss, but each IsI_s is convex in CC at its own fixed input law, so the nonnegative combination is convex in CC. Linearity of the distortion is immediate.

Lemma 23 (The tilt root: existence, interiority, uniqueness).

Fix p∈(0,12)p\in(0,\tfrac12), q∈(0,12]q\in(0,\tfrac12], D∈(0,12)D\in(0,\tfrac12). Parameterize the constraint segment (1−p)d0+pd1=D(1-p)d_0+pd_1=D, (d0,d1)∈(0,1)2(d_0,d_1)\in(0,1)^2, by d0∈(max⁡{0,D−p1−p},D1−p)d_0\in\bigl(\max\{0,\tfrac{D-p}{1-p}\},\ \tfrac{D}{1-p}\bigr), an open subinterval of (0,1)(0,1), and define the tilt residual ψ(d0):=ℓ(d0)−ℓ(d1(d0))−2(1−2q)ℓ(u(d0)),\psi(d_0):=\ell(d_0)-\ell\bigl(d_1(d_0)\bigr) -2(1-2q)\,\ell\bigl(u(d_0)\bigr), d1(d0)=D−(1−p)d0p,u=a*q,a=2(1−p)d0+p−D.d_1(d_0)=\frac{D-(1-p)d_0}{p},\qquad u=a*q,\qquad a=2(1-p)d_0+p-D . Then ψ\psi has exactly one zero on the open segment, and the family value L(d0)L(d_0) attains its minimum over the closed segment exactly there. The same statements hold at q=0q=0 when D<pD<p.

Proof. Work in nats; L(d0)=H(u)−(1−p)H(d0)−pH(d1(d0))L(d_0)=H(u)-(1-p)H(d_0)-pH\bigl(d_1(d_0)\bigr) with HH the natural-log binary entropy. Differentiating with H′(x)=ℓ(x)H'(x)=\ell(x), u′(d0)=2(1−p)(1−2q)u'(d_0)=2(1-p)(1-2q), and d1′(d0)=−(1−p)/pd_1'(d_0)=-(1-p)/p, L′(d0)=2(1−p)(1−2q)ℓ(u)−(1−p)ℓ(d0)+(1−p)ℓ(d1)=−(1−p)ψ(d0).L'(d_0)=2(1-p)(1-2q)\,\ell(u)-(1-p)\,\ell(d_0)+(1-p)\,\ell(d_1) =-(1-p)\,\psi(d_0).

Existence and interiority. Boundary behavior. At the left endpoint: if D≤pD\le p the endpoint is d0=0d_0=0 and ℓ(d0)→+∞\ell(d_0)\to+\infty; if additionally D=pD=p then also d1→1d_1\to1 and −ℓ(d1)→+∞-\ell(d_1)\to+\infty, the same sign; if D>pD>p the endpoint is d0=(D−p)/(1−p)>0d_0=(D-p)/(1-p)>0 with d1→1d_1\to1, so −ℓ(d1)→+∞-\ell(d_1)\to+\infty with the other terms bounded. The uu term stays bounded in every case: u=a*q∈[q,1−q]u=a*q\in[q,1-q] with q>0q>0. Hence ψ→+∞\psi\to+\infty at the left endpoint. At the right endpoint d0=D/(1−p)<1d_0=D/(1-p)<1 (since 1−p>12>D1-p>\tfrac12>D): d1→0d_1\to0, so −ℓ(d1)→−∞-\ell(d_1)\to-\infty with the other terms bounded, and ψ→−∞\psi\to-\infty. ψ\psi is continuous on the open segment, so it has a zero there by the intermediate value theorem, and trivially every zero is interior.

Zeros are minimizers. The family channel is affine in (d0,d1)(d_0,d_1), hence affine in d0d_0 along the segment, and LL is convex in the channel (Lemma 22), so LL is convex on the segment. For a convex differentiable function, L′(d0)=0L'(d_0)=0 at an interior point makes that point a global minimizer; conversely L′→−∞L'\to-\infty at the left endpoint and L′→+∞L'\to+\infty at the right (the sign flips of ψ\psi), so the minimum of LL over the closed segment is attained in the interior and only at zeros of ψ\psi.

Uniqueness. The minimizer set of the convex LL is a closed interval on which LL is constant. Suppose it contains two distinct points. Then L″≡0L''\equiv0 on a nondegenerate subinterval. But LL is real analytic on the open segment: d1d_1 and aa are affine in d0d_0 with values in (0,1)(0,1), u=a(1−2q)+q∈(0,1)u=a(1-2q)+q\in(0,1), and HH is real analytic on (0,1)(0,1). By the identity theorem, L″≡0L''\equiv0 on the whole connected open segment, so L′L' is constant there, contradicting L′→−∞L'\to-\infty at the left endpoint. Hence the minimizer is unique, and since the zeros of ψ\psi are exactly the interior stationary points of LL, which are exactly its minimizers, ψ\psi has exactly one zero.

At q=0q=0 with D<pD<p the same argument applies verbatim: the left endpoint is d0=0d_0=0 with d1(0)=D/p<1d_1(0)=D/p<1, and u=a∈(p−D,p+D)⊂(0,1)u=a\in(p-D,p+D)\subset (0,1) stays bounded away from 00 and 11, so the boundary blow-ups and the analyticity are as before.

For q∈(0,12]q\in(0,\tfrac12] and D<12D<\tfrac12, L(D)>0L(D)>0.

Proof. Reduction and convexity. Binary Ŷ\hat Y is definitional (DPI above); convexity of LL in the shared channel and linearity of the distortion are Lemma 22.

Symmetrization. The global bit flip σ:(y,v,s,ŷ)↦(1−y,1−v,1−s,1−ŷ)\sigma:(y,v,s,\hat y)\mapsto(1{-}y,1{-}v,1{-}s,1{-}\hat y) preserves the joint law of (Y,V,S)(Y,V,S): the pair (Y,V)(Y,V) is doubly symmetric with fair marginals, so (1−Y,1−V)=d(Y,V)(1{-}Y,1{-}V)\overset{d}=(Y,V), and W∼Bern(q)W\sim \mathrm{Bern}(q) is independent of (Y,V)(Y,V), so S=V⊕WS=V\oplus W flips with VV. The flip also preserves the distortion, and L(Cσ)=L(C)L(C^\sigma)=L(C); averaging CC with CσC^\sigma preserves distortion and, by convexity, does not increase LL. So an optimum exists among σ\sigma-symmetric channels, and these are exactly the family {(d0,d1)}\{(d_0,d_1)\}: σ\sigma-symmetry forces Pr⁡[Ŷ≠Y∣y,v]\Pr[\hat Y\ne Y\mid y,v] to depend only on y⊕vy\oplus v.

Closed form. On the family, H(Ŷ∣Y,V)=(1−p)h2(d0)+ph2(d1)H(\hat Y\mid Y,V)= (1-p)h_2(d_0)+p\,h_2(d_1), and Ŷ⊕S=J⊕E⊕W\hat Y\oplus S=J\oplus E\oplus W (J=Y⊕VJ=Y\oplus V) with Pr⁡[J⊕E=1]=a\Pr[J\oplus E=1]=a. The step H(Ŷ∣S)=h2(a*q)H(\hat Y\mid S)=h_2(a*q) needs Ŷ⊕S⟂S\hat Y\oplus S\perp S, which holds because the joint law of (Ŷ,S)(\hat Y,S) is σ\sigma-invariant (σ\sigma-invariant source, σ\sigma-symmetric channel), forcing equal conditional flip probabilities given either value of SS; the same symmetry gives H(Ŷ)=1H(\hat Y)=1, hence RR.

Tilt equation. Substituting d1=(D−(1−p)d0)/pd_1=(D-(1-p)d_0)/p makes a=2(1−p)d0+p−Da=2(1-p)d_0+p-D affine in d0d_0; differentiating LL and using h2′(x)=ℓ(x)h_2'(x)=\ell(x) (nats) gives (1−p)[2(1−2q)ℓ(u)−ℓ(d0)+ℓ(d1)]=0(1-p)[2(1-2q)\ell(u)-\ell(d_0)+\ell(d_1)]=0. Since LL restricted to the affine family slice is convex (restriction of a convex function), interior stationarity is sufficient, not merely necessary.

Anchors and positivity. q=12q=\tfrac12: u=12u=\tfrac12, the tilt equation forces d0=d1=Dd_0=d_1=D. q=0q=0: substitution of Gray’s backward channel; equality of values is elementary algebra. Positivity, in two branches over the family (which suffices by attainment): if a≠12a\ne\tfrac12, then h2(u)>h2(a)≥(1−p)h2(d0)+ph2(1−d1)=(1−p)h2(d0)+ph2(d1)h_2(u)>h_2(a)\ge(1-p)h_2(d_0)+p\,h_2(1-d_1) =(1-p)h_2(d_0)+p\,h_2(d_1), where the strict step holds because u=a*qu=a*q is strictly closer to 12\tfrac12 for q∈(0,12]q\in(0,\tfrac12] and the second step by concavity; so L>0L>0. If a=12a=\tfrac12, then u=12u=\tfrac12, h2(u)=1h_2(u)=1, and L=1−(1−p)h2(d0)−ph2(d1)≥1−h2(D)>0L=1-(1-p)h_2(d_0)-p\,h_2(d_1)\ge1-h_2(D)>0 by concavity at the distortion.

□

Reproduction alphabets larger than binary are already covered by the data-processing reduction that opens this section; no separate argument is needed for them. The unconditional Lagrangian bounds, which assume no convexity, numerically re-confirm that reduction and the family-plus-tilt optimum.

Remark 25 (The binary rate–content frontier). The symmetric family exhausts not only the conditional coordinate but the entire rate–content frontier at distortion DD. The rate coordinate R=I(Y,V;Ŷ)R=I(Y,V;\hat Y) is convex in the shared channel by the argument of Lemma 22 with the trivial conditioner, so every weighted objective αR+(1−α)L\alpha R+(1-\alpha)L, α∈[0,1]\alpha\in[0,1], is convex in the channel. The global bit flip σ\sigma of Theorem 24’s proof preserves the joint law of (Y,V,S)(Y,V,S), the distortion, and both coordinates: the flip is a law-preserving bijective relabeling of both arguments of each mutual information, so R(Cσ)=R(C)R(C^\sigma)=R(C) and L(Cσ)=L(C)L(C^\sigma)=L(C). Averaging a channel with its flip therefore preserves the distortion and, by convexity, does not increase any weighted objective, and larger reproduction alphabets are covered by the data-processing reduction in both coordinates. Every weighted optimum is thus attained in the family {(d0,d1)}\{(d_0,d_1)\}, and the distortion constraint may be taken active there: both coordinates are nonnegative and vanish at d0=d1=12d_0=d_1=\tfrac12, so by convexity the objective does not increase along the straight path from any point with distortion slack toward (12,12)(\tfrac12,\tfrac12), while the distortion, affine in (d0,d1)(d_0,d_1) with positive weights, rises continuously to 12>D\tfrac12>D and meets the budget on the way. The Pareto frontier of the binary rate–content region at distortion DD is therefore the lower-left envelope of the curve d0↦(R(d0),L(d0)),R(d0)=1−(1−p)h2(d0)−ph2(d1(d0)),d_0\;\longmapsto\;\bigl(R(d_0),\,L(d_0)\bigr), \qquad R(d_0)=1-(1-p)\,h_2(d_0)-p\,h_2\bigl(d_1(d_0)\bigr), along the constraint segment. On the segment, RR is strictly convex with its unique minimum at d0=d1=Dd_0=d_1=D (strict concavity of (1−p)h2(d0)+ph2(d1)(1-p)h_2(d_0)+p\,h_2(d_1) and the stationarity ℓ(d0)=ℓ(d1)\ell(d_0)=\ell(d_1)), where R=1−h2(D)R=1-h_2(D), the marginal rate–distortion function; LL has its unique minimum at the tilt root d0⋆d_0^\star (Lemma 23). For q∈(0,12)q\in(0,\tfrac12) the two minimizers are distinct, since ψ(D)=−2(1−2q)ℓ(u(D))<0\psi(D)=-2(1-2q)\,\ell\bigl(u(D)\bigr)<0 (there u(D)<12u(D)<\tfrac12 because a(D)=p+D(1−2p)<12a(D)=p+D(1-2p)<\tfrac12), so d0⋆<Dd_0^\star<D: on [d0⋆,D][d_0^\star,D] the curve is a strict tradeoff arc, LL increasing and RR decreasing, and outside that arc both coordinates worsen. At q=12q=\tfrac12 the two minimizers coincide at d0=Dd_0=D and the frontier is a single corner. Fig. 3 traces the frontier at a representative instance.

The nearest published binary calculations are common-reconstruction functions with decoder side information. Steinberg’s binary example [12] evaluates the constrained functional for a binary symmetric pair: the decoder’s side information is the source through a binary symmetric channel, the distortion is Hamming, the optimal reverse test channel is a BSC of crossover DD independent of the pair correlation, and the value is h2(ρ0*D)−h2(D)h_2(\rho_0*D)-h_2(D) at side-channel crossover ρ0\rho_0. Ahmadi, Tandon, Simeone, and Poor [14] computed common-reconstruction functions for a binary source with erased side information under Hamming and erasure distortion, in point-to-point, Heegard–Berger, and cascade configurations; the point-to-point value is pe(1−h2(D))p_e(1-h_2(D)) at erasure rate pep_e. Both computations live in the decoder-side-information setting: SS sits at the decoder, the encoder observes the source alone, and the common-reconstruction constraint disciplines how the decoder may use SS. Theorem 24 differs structurally. Here SS is held by a third party that never decodes, the encoder observes the pair (Y,V)(Y,V), and the constraint binds the unconditional Hamming error Pr⁡[Ŷ≠Y]\Pr[\hat Y\ne Y]. The function is anchored at Gray’s conditional function at q=0q=0 and at the marginal rate–distortion function at q=12q=\tfrac12, an interpolation with no counterpart in the decoder-side calculations. An encoder restricted to YY alone faces exactly the constrained problem of the pair (Y,S)(Y,S), a binary symmetric pair with crossover p*qp*q, and pays Steinberg’s value there (the marginalization identity of Section IV is alphabet-free); the tilt equation is the price of pair access.

IX. Discussion and Conclusion

This paper characterized the minimal conditional content of a description whose encoder observes the pair (Y,V)(Y,V) while the conditioner SS stays with a third party: the closed form of Theorem 11 for YY and VV scalar linear functionals of an arbitrary-dimensional jointly Gaussian source, the exact rate–content region of Theorem 13 with its two-water-level frontier and the misalignment dichotomy of Corollary 16, the determinant-bound attainment condition of Theorem 20, the vector-context extension of Theorem 21, and the complete binary solution of Theorem 24. The function degenerates to the classical rate–distortion function at ρ=0\rho=0 and to Gray’s conditional function as τ2→0\tau^2\to0, and meets Steinberg’s scalar Gaussian formula at the ρ2→1\rho^2\to1 boundary. The structural moral is Corollary 18: the function is not determined by the reduced marginal (Y,S)(Y,S) but by what the encoder can see, so conditional description content is a property of the encoding configuration, not of the source and side-information pair alone.

The thermodynamic reading is fixed by the operational theorem of Section II: L(D)L(D) is the minimal ideal erasure work per symbol, in units of kBTln⁡2k_{\mathrm{B}}T\ln2, paid by a reset mechanism that retains SS [24], [26], [27]. The region states when storing cheaply and erasing cheaply are compatible: at ρ=0\rho=0 one channel minimizes both coordinates, and under misalignment (ρ2∈(0,1)\rho^2\in(0,1), τ2>0\tau^2>0) the two costs strictly trade off.

The same asymmetry, descriptions read by parties whose requirements they were not sized to, extends beyond source coding. In companion empirical work by the author, the operational failure rate of decisions made from stale or mismatched descriptions plays the role that LL plays here as an information price. The misaligned regime τ2>0\tau^2>0 is exactly the regime such measurements probe; we claim no equivalence beyond this correspondence of roles.

Four problems are open. The exact rate–content region for a joint description serving two described variables is not settled; its stationarity system is known in necessary-condition form only. The analogous function for a described variable of dimension greater than one is open. Stationary sources, and the process and spectral versions of the function, are not treated here. The finite-blocklength behavior of the pair (Rn,Ln)(R_n,L_n) is unexplored.

Everything in this paper is single-letter and memoryless, Gaussian and binary. Every closed form is verified by the independent numerical checks of Appendix C.

Appendix A: Single-Letterization

For completeness, we justify the last inequalities in (13) and (14). For the rate coordinate, I(Xn;X̂n)=H(Xn)−H(Xn∣X̂n)=∑i=1nH(Xi)−∑i=1nH(Xi∣Xi−1,X̂n)≥∑i=1n[H(Xi)−H(Xi∣X̂i)]=∑i=1nI(Xi;X̂i).(45)\begin{align*} I(X^n;\widehat{X}^{n}) &=H(X^n)-H(X^n\mid\widehat{X}^{n})\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(X_i) -\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(X_i\mid X^{i-1},\widehat{X}^{n})\\ &\ge\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left[H(X_i)-H(X_i\mid\widehat{X}_i)\right]\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^{n}I(X_i;\widehat{X}_i). \qquad\text{(45)} \end{align*} For the work coordinate, I(Xn;X̂n∣Sn)=H(Xn∣Sn)−H(Xn∣X̂n,Sn)=∑i=1nH(Xi∣Si)−∑i=1nH(Xi∣Xi−1,X̂n,Sn)≥∑i=1n[H(Xi∣Si)−H(Xi∣X̂i,Si)]=∑i=1nI(Xi;X̂i∣Si).(46)\begin{align*} I(X^n;\widehat{X}^{n}\mid S^n) &=H(X^n\mid S^n)-H(X^n\mid\widehat{X}^{n},S^n)\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(X_i\mid S_i) -\sum_{i=1}^{n}H(X_i\mid X^{i-1},\widehat{X}^{n},S^n)\\ &\ge\sum_{i=1}^{n} \left[H(X_i\mid S_i)-H(X_i\mid\widehat{X}_i,S_i)\right]\\ &=\sum_{i=1}^{n}I(X_i;\widehat{X}_i\mid S_i). \qquad\text{(46)} \end{align*}

Appendix B: The Gaussian Operational Theorem

This appendix proves the operational region theorem for the jointly Gaussian source of Section III, replacing the customary appeal to an unspecified abstract-alphabet extension. The source letter is X=(Y,V)X=(Y,V), jointly Gaussian; the conditioner is SS as in Section III or Section VII; the distortion is d(x,ŷ)=(y−ŷ)2d(x,\hat y)=(y-\hat y)^2, unbounded; codes, RnR_n, DnD_n, and Ln=H(M∣Sn)/nL_n=H(M\mid S^n)/n are as in Section II, and achievability is Definition 1.

Two devices are fixed first. The saturating dyadic quantizers: for k≥1k\ge1, let qkq_k partition ℝ\mathbb{R} into the bounded cells [j2−k,(j+1)2−k)[j2^{-k},(j+1)2^{-k}), −4k≤j<4k-4^k\le j<4^k, together with the two saturating tail cells (−∞,−2k)(-\infty,-2^k) and [2k,∞)[2^k,\infty); for a vector conditioner S∈ℝrS\in\mathbb{R}^r, apply qkq_k to each coordinate, so the cells are rectangles. The partitions are nested, every cell edge of qkq_k being an edge of qk+1q_{k+1}, so the generated σ\sigma-fields σ(qk(S))\sigma(q_k(S)) increase, and their union generates the Borel σ\sigma-field of SS, since the dyadic intervals do. Write Sk:=qk(S)S_k:=q_k(S). The second device is an integrability bound for the quantized pair.

Lemma 26 (Cell bound). Let (Ŷ,S)(\widehat{Y},S) be jointly Gaussian, Ŷ\widehat{Y} scalar and centered, S∈ℝrS\in\mathbb{R}^r, with ΣS∣Ŷ≻0\Sigma_{S\mid\widehat{Y}}\succ0, and fix kk. For every cell AA of the product quantizer qkq_k there is a constant CA<∞C_A<\infty such that |ln⁡Pr⁡(S∈A∣Ŷ=ŷ)Pr⁡(S∈A)|≤CA(1+ŷ2)for every ŷ∈ℝ.\Bigl|\,\ln\frac{\Pr(S\in A\mid\widehat{Y}=\hat y)}{\Pr(S\in A)}\Bigr| \;\le\;C_A\bigl(1+\hat y^{\,2}\bigr) \qquad\text{for every }\hat y\in\mathbb{R}. Consequently the information density of the pair (Ŷ,Sk)(\widehat{Y},S_k) is bounded in magnitude by a fixed quadratic in ŷ\hat y, and has finite moments of all orders.

Proof. The conditional law of SS given Ŷ=ŷ\widehat{Y}=\hat y is Gaussian with mean mŷm\hat y linear in ŷ\hat y and fixed covariance Σ̃:=ΣS∣Ŷ≻0\widetilde\Sigma:=\Sigma_{S\mid\widehat{Y}}\succ0; the marginal of SS is Gaussian with covariance ΣS≻0\Sigma_S\succ0.

Scalar SS, bounded cells. For a bounded cell A=[u,v)A=[u,v), the ratio of the two integrals lies between the infimum and the supremum over AA of the integrand ratio r(u′,ŷ):=fS∣Ŷ(u′∣ŷ)/fS(u′)r(u',\hat y):=f_{S\mid\widehat{Y}}(u'\mid\hat y)/f_S(u'), so |ln⁡(Pr⁡(A∣ŷ)/Pr⁡(A))|≤sup⁡u′∈A|ln⁡r(u′,ŷ)||\ln(\Pr(A\mid\hat y)/\Pr(A))|\le\sup_{u'\in A}|\ln r(u',\hat y)|. Here ln⁡r(u′,ŷ)=ln⁡σSσ̃−(u′−mŷ)22σ̃2+u′22σS2,\ln r(u',\hat y) =\ln\frac{\sigma_S}{\widetilde\sigma} -\frac{(u'-m\hat y)^2}{2\widetilde\sigma^2} +\frac{u'^2}{2\sigma_S^2}, a quadratic in (u′,ŷ)(u',\hat y); taking the supremum over the bounded range u′∈[u,v)u'\in[u,v) leaves a quadratic in ŷ\hat y with coefficients determined by the cell endpoints, which is the claimed bound.

Scalar SS, tail cells. For A=[2k,∞)A=[2^k,\infty), Pr⁡(A∣ŷ)=Φ¯((2k−mŷ)/σ̃)\Pr(A\mid\hat y)=\overline\Phi\bigl((2^k-m\hat y)/\widetilde\sigma\bigr) and Pr⁡(A)=Φ¯(2k/σS)\Pr(A)=\overline\Phi(2^k/\sigma_S), a constant, where Φ¯\overline\Phi is the standard Gaussian tail. The elementary bound |ln⁡Φ¯(z)|≤C(1+z2)|\ln\overline\Phi(z)|\le C(1+z^2) holds on all of ℝ\mathbb{R}: for z≤0z\le0, Φ¯(z)∈[12,1)\overline\Phi(z)\in[\tfrac12,1); for 0<z≤10<z\le1, Φ¯(z)∈[Φ¯(1),12)\overline\Phi(z)\in[\overline\Phi(1),\tfrac12); and for z>1z>1 the Mills-ratio bounds zφ(z)/(1+z2)≤Φ¯(z)≤φ(z)/zz\varphi(z)/(1+z^2)\le\overline\Phi(z)\le\varphi(z)/z give |ln⁡Φ¯(z)|≤z2/2+ln⁡2π+ln⁡(2z)|\ln\overline\Phi(z)|\le z^2/2+\ln\sqrt{2\pi}+\ln(2z). The information density of (Ŷ,Sk)(\widehat{Y},S_k) at (ŷ,j)(\hat y,j) is ln⁡[Pr⁡(Sk=j∣ŷ)/Pr⁡(Sk=j)]\ln[\Pr(S_k=j\mid\hat y)/\Pr(S_k=j)]; taking C:=max⁡jCAjC:=\max_jC_{A_j} over the finitely many cells bounds it by C(1+ŷ2)C(1+\hat y^{\,2}), which has finite moments of all orders under the Gaussian law of Ŷ\widehat{Y}.

Theorem 27 (Extension: the Gaussian operational region). For the Gaussian source and every 0<D<10<D<1, ℛ𝒲(D)=⋃p(ŷ∣x):𝔼(Y−Ŷ)2≤D{(R,L):R≥I(X;Ŷ),L≥I(X;Ŷ∣S)},\mathcal{R}\!\mathcal{W}(D)=\bigcup_{p(\hat y\mid x):\,\mathbb{E}(Y-\widehat{Y})^2\le D} \bigl\{(R,L):R\ge I(X;\widehat{Y}),\ L\ge I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S)\bigr\}, and the union is unchanged when restricted to jointly Gaussian test channels. For D≥1D\ge1 the result follows from the zero reproduction, which meets the distortion constraint with R=L=0R=L=0; the point D=0D=0 follows as the extended-real limiting case, both coordinates diverging. Throughout, LnL_n is a coding quantity, the normalized conditional entropy of the stored index; its thermodynamic reading is the idealized bound (7), and no step of the proof depends on that reading.

Proof. Converse. The chain of Theorem 4’s converse (the discrete operational region theorem) holds verbatim with differential entropies for the continuous source. MM is discrete, so log⁡|ℳn|≥H(M)≥I(Xn;M)≥I(Xn;Ŷn)\log|\mathcal M_n|\ge H(M)\ge I(X^n;M)\ge I(X^n;\widehat{Y}^n) and H(M∣Sn)≥I(Xn;M∣Sn)≥I(Xn;Ŷn∣Sn)H(M\mid S^n)\ge I(X^n;M\mid S^n)\ge I(X^n;\widehat{Y}^n\mid S^n) are unchanged. Restriction to Gaussian channels. For any admissible channel, Lemma 9 (Gaussian exhaustion: the two determinant lower bounds, met with equality by the jointly Gaussian channel matching the second moments) produces the jointly Gaussian channel with the same second moments and the same distortion, whose coordinates I(X;Ŷ)I(X;\widehat{Y}) and I(X;Ŷ∣S)I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S) are componentwise no larger than the original channel’s. Its quadrant therefore contains the original channel’s quadrant, so the union over all channels equals the union over jointly Gaussian channels. It thus suffices to prove achievability for a jointly Gaussian test channel.

Achievability, Step A: quantizing the conditioner. Fix a jointly Gaussian admissible channel p(ŷ∣x)p(\hat y\mid x) with distortion at most DD, and fix ϵ>0\epsilon>0. Along the saturating dyadic quantizers, I(Ŷ;Sk)↑I(Ŷ;S)(k→∞):(47)\begin{equation*} I(\widehat{Y};S_k)\;\uparrow\;I(\widehat{Y};S)\qquad(k\to\infty): \qquad\text{(47)} \end{equation*} the sequence is nondecreasing because the partitions are nested (data processing), and its supremum is I(Ŷ;S)I(\widehat{Y};S) by monotone convergence of mutual information under σ\sigma-fields increasing to the Borel σ\sigma-field of SS [7, Ch. 2]: mutual information is the supremum of the mutual informations of finite measurable partitions of the two sample spaces, and every finite Borel partition of the SS-space is approximated, up to sets of arbitrarily small measure, by partitions measurable with respect to some σ(Sk)\sigma(S_k). Choose kk with I(Ŷ;SΔ)≥I(Ŷ;S)−ϵ,SΔ:=Sk.(48)\begin{equation*} I(\widehat{Y};S_\Delta)\;\ge\;I(\widehat{Y};S)-\epsilon, \qquad S_\Delta:=S_k . \qquad\text{(48)} \end{equation*} SΔS_\Delta is a function of SS, so the Markov chain Ŷ−X−SΔ\widehat{Y}-X-S_\Delta holds, and by the chain-rule identity used throughout (I(X;Ŷ)−I(X;Ŷ∣S′)=I(Ŷ;S′)I(X;\widehat{Y})-I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S')=I(\widehat{Y};S') for any conditioner S′S' with Ŷ−X−S′\widehat{Y}-X-S'), I(X;Ŷ∣SΔ)=I(X;Ŷ)−I(Ŷ;SΔ)≤I(X;Ŷ∣S)+ϵ.(49)\begin{equation*} I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S_\Delta)=I(X;\widehat{Y})-I(\widehat{Y};S_\Delta) \;\le\;I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S)+\epsilon . \qquad\text{(49)} \end{equation*}

Achievability, Step B: coding against the quantized conditioner. The pair source is now (X,SΔ)(X,S_\Delta) with continuous XX and finite SΔS_\Delta. Build the code of Theorem 4’s achievability proof (covering, binning, and expurgation, as in the discrete theorem) for this pair: a codebook of 2n(I(X;Ŷ)+2ϵ)2^{n(I(X;\widehat{Y})+2\epsilon)} codewords drawn from the Ŷ\widehat{Y}-marginal with quadratic-distortion covering, a uniform random binning at rate I(X;Ŷ∣SΔ)+3ϵI(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S_\Delta)+3\epsilon, and the side-information proof device decoding MM from (B,SΔn)(B,S_\Delta^n). Two classical probabilistic ingredients are imported. The covering step is Gaussian quadratic-distortion achievability for an arbitrary jointly Gaussian test channel, the Gaussian source coding theorem with the backward-channel argument [2]. The side-information step, the joint typicality of the selected codeword with the memoryless side information (the Markov lemma) together with the packing bound for wrong codewords in a bin, is the abstract-alphabet analysis of Wyner [6]. That analysis needs only that the per-letter information densities of the pairs (X,Ŷ)(X,\widehat{Y}) and (Ŷ,SΔ)(\widehat{Y},S_\Delta) be integrable, so that they obey the law of large numbers and the density-typical sets carry the standard change-of-measure bounds. Both conditions hold here: the (X,Ŷ)(X,\widehat{Y}) density is a quadratic polynomial in (x,ŷ)(x,\hat y) for the jointly Gaussian pair, and the (Ŷ,SΔ)(\widehat{Y},S_\Delta) density is bounded by a fixed quadratic in ŷ\hat y, with finite moments of all orders, by Lemma 26. Everything else, in particular the expurgation selecting one deterministic (codebook, binning) pair meeting the distortion and the conditional-entropy requirements simultaneously, is the argument written out in Theorem 4’s proof, verbatim (the distortion excess on the covering-failure event is controlled by the uniformly integrable quadratic distortion of the Gaussian pair in place of dmaxd_{\max}: encode the failure event by the zero codeword, whose per-letter distortion has fixed finite mean, so a vanishing failure probability contributes o(1)o(1) to DnD_n by Cauchy–Schwarz). The selected code has rate I(X;Ŷ)+2ϵI(X;\widehat{Y})+2\epsilon, distortion at most D+ϵ+o(1)D+\epsilon+o(1), and H(M∣SΔn)≤n(I(X;Ŷ∣SΔ)+3ϵ+o(1)).(50)\begin{equation*} H(M\mid S_\Delta^n)\;\le\; n\bigl(I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S_\Delta)+3\epsilon+o(1)\bigr). \qquad\text{(50)} \end{equation*}

Achievability, Step C: back to the unquantized conditioner. SΔnS_\Delta^n is a function of SnS^n, so σ(SΔn)⊆σ(Sn)\sigma(S_\Delta^n)\subseteq\sigma(S^n) and conditioning on the finer σ\sigma-algebra cannot increase entropy: H(M∣Sn)≤H(M∣SΔn)≤n(I(X;Ŷ∣SΔ)+3ϵ+o(1))≤n(I(X;Ŷ∣S)+4ϵ+o(1)),(51)\begin{equation*} H(M\mid S^n)\;\le\;H(M\mid S_\Delta^n) \;\le\;n\bigl(I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S_\Delta)+3\epsilon+o(1)\bigr) \;\le\;n\bigl(I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S)+4\epsilon+o(1)\bigr), \qquad\text{(51)} \end{equation*} by (50) and (49).

Collect. For every ϵ>0\epsilon>0 the triple (I(X;Ŷ)+2ϵ,I(X;Ŷ∣S)+4ϵ,D+ϵ)\bigl(I(X;\widehat{Y})+2\epsilon,\ I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S)+4\epsilon,\ D+\epsilon\bigr) is achievable; a diagonal sequence ϵj↓0\epsilon_j\downarrow0 of codes achieves, in the limsup\limsup sense of Definition 1, the corner (I(X;Ŷ),I(X;Ŷ∣S))\bigl(I(X;\widehat{Y}),I(X;\widehat{Y}\mid S)\bigr) at distortion DD, and the quadrant above the corner is immediate from the definition. Together with the converse and the restriction step, this proves the theorem.

□

The imports are stated for the record: Gaussian quadratic-distortion covering [2] and Wyner’s abstract-alphabet side-information analysis [6] are classical, predate this work, and are logically independent of the present results; every other step is proved here or in Section II.

Appendix C: Numerical Verification

Each closed form and each displayed matrix identity was checked independently of the derivations, symbolically by exact computer algebra and numerically against direct optimization over test-channel moments, twice over: by the author’s harness, written alongside the proofs, and by a separately commissioned re-derivation, archived with the repository. All checks pass. The load-bearing scalar algebra is additionally machine-checked in two further engines, a Lean 4/Mathlib module built clean with zero sorry and the MATLAB Symbolic toolbox. The matrix-general exhaustion lemma, the measure-theoretic steps (single-letterization, covering and binning, disintegration), the matrix-convexity lemma, the uniqueness proposition, and the binary theorem’s symmetrization and positivity arguments are verified by written proof and the numerical harnesses, not by the proof assistant. The scripts, their archived run outputs, and the full check inventory accompany the manuscript sources at the repository of the title footnote (VERIFICATION.md in the paper directory). Table III summarizes the main checks.
